notes: Full sweep 2026-10-31: five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2). Each result.json has head 0814e8d, uncommitted false, skill_hash 38869366..., rc 0, model_id equal to the requested model, files [review.md], and reads SKILL.md, ecto-phoenix.md, processes.md (opus-1 also library-design.md). Every assistant message in each transcript reports only the run's model. Each transcript contains the current text of the changed rules (for example "read a key it must hold with", "A line break is not decomposition", "A pipeline never sits on one line", "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance"), so the runs read the current skill. All five read both expected reference files before writing review.md (haiku-2 also read SKILL.md with `cat`, sonnet-2 read both references with one `cat`). Each run's code-review-input.ex equals evals/cases/code-review-input.ex. Opus-1 built a test project inside its run folder and deleted it before finishing; haiku-2's and sonnet-2's scratch writes were refused, and both said so. result.json has no format_ok field, so format_ok comes from this grade's own check.

Rule list: 16 index rows name code-review, the 15 of the 2026-10-23 grade plus the new 'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression' (index cell: not yet graded). Rule text: git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes four rules in the list. (1) 'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression' is new. (2) The pipeline rule's first bullet gains the never-on-one-line, plain-nested-call and mode-argument sentences. (3) 'Match every expected shape...' gains the `elem/2` sentence and reformats its examples. (4) The required-keys rule gains the `Keyword.fetch!/2` sentence. Outside the list, the `with` rule now allows a one-step pass-through `with`, the `do:`, captures and multi-line-argument rules are rewritten, the `->` rule and 'One expression per line, and tabular clauses' are new, the configuration rule gains a module-attribute sentence, and ex_unit.md, library-design.md, macros.md and processes.md change examples or wording. The 12 unchanged graded rules are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. A problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under behaviour changes or assumptions, does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'. The comments, both magic numbers and a dropped line 11 why-comment belong to 'Comments explain why...', and a fix of `min(age, 120)` does not report the 120. Input lines 12 and 55 belong to the pipeline rule. The line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors belong to 'Match every expected shape'; a finding that treats the rescue only as hiding bugs does not count for the identical errors. The line 8 raise outside the `try` belongs to 'Return {:ok, value}...'. The dead `is_binary` belongs to no rule. A one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body is not nesting. A `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted. `Map.get/2` on a struct breaks the required-keys rule. An assumed or companion changeset counts as a changeset.

Deciding sentences for the changed rules. 'Name a step instead of wrapping an expression': clean in all five, decided by "A binding earns its place when it names a recognizable thing or a stage of the computation, holds a value used more than once, ..." and "It does not when it only renames a value used once (...), when the nested call is plain (...)". Every binding in the five outputs names a stage or a value: the built message or email each closure captures (opus-1 `message`, line 112; haiku-1 and haiku-2 `email`, lines 70/71; sonnet-1 `email`, line 141; sonnet-2 `welcome_email`, line 121), the changeset (haiku-1 line 61, haiku-2 line 62), a computed default (opus-1 `nickname`, line 107; haiku-2 and opus-1 `name`), sonnet-1's lowercased `email` used twice (lines 123, 126, 129) and the sonnets' multi-line `attrs` map. The plain nested calls stay nested: opus-1 line 88 `Repo.insert(import_changeset(params))`, and haiku-1 line 105 and haiku-2 line 104 `put_change(changeset, :nickname, get_field(changeset, :email))`. No output has an expression that is only wrapped across lines, so the sentence "A line break is not decomposition" is not exercised. Pipeline rule: decided, as before, by the unchanged "Do not pipe a single step" bullet, through sonnet-2's unreported input line 12. The new "A pipeline never sits on one line" and "An argument that only selects a kind or a mode does not start a pipeline" are not exercised: no output has a one-line pipeline, and every pipeline starts with `%User{}`, `user` or a changeset, one step per line. 'Match every expected shape...': the new "The same goes for `elem/2` on a tuple whose shape is known" is not exercised, since no output calls `elem/2`. The verdicts come from the unchanged identical-errors standard and the first paragraph. Required keys: the new sentence "A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`, ..., and keep `opts[:key]` for an option that has a default" keeps every run's `opts[:notify]` (opus-1 line 84, haiku-1 line 64, sonnet-1 line 100 and sonnet-2 line 81 after `Keyword.validate!(opts, notify: false)`; haiku-2 line 65 with `false` documented as the default). Haiku-2's violation is decided by the unchanged "Structs do not implement `Access`: ..., so read struct fields with `user.name` or a pattern", against its line 76 `Map.get(user, :name)`. Sonnet-1's body reads `params["email"]` and `params["role"]` (lines 123, 128) after its head has matched both keys. Those cannot be nil, and the rule's sentences are about atom keys and structs, so they are not counted, as the 2026-10-23 baseline grade did not count body string reads.

Planted problems, mapped as in the 2026-10-23 grades: 21 problems from the case table's 19 rows, with the line 15-17 rebinding counted apart from the magic 120, and the line 49 spawn apart from the closure copy. Counts: opus-1 21/21. Haiku-1 17/21, missing the line 8 raise outside the `try`, the dead `is_binary`, the magic 18 and the identical errors. Haiku-2 15/21, missing the line 8 raise, the nesting, both magic numbers, the identical errors and the closure copy. Sonnet-1 18/21, missing both magic numbers (finding 3's fix keeps `min(age, 120)`) and the identical errors. Sonnet-2 19/21, missing the line 12 single-step pipe and the magic 18. All five report the line 24 lookup-before-insert with the race and drop `Repo.get_by/2` for `unique_constraint(:email)`: opus-1 finding 4, haiku-1 finding 5, haiku-2 finding 5, sonnet-1 finding 5 and sonnet-2 finding 6.

Judgment calls on 'reported'. Opus-1's identical errors count through finding 4 ("A duplicate is also reported as `{:error, :invalid}`, the same as bad input."), as the 2026-10-23 baseline grade counted a sonnet-1 finding that a duplicate returns `:invalid`. Sonnet-2's count, borderline, through finding 2 ("turns a `nil` email, a bad age and a database crash into the same `:invalid`"), as 2026-10-23 counted its sonnet-2 finding 2. Haiku-1's finding 3 ("hide every failure, including a database error in `Repo.insert`, and report it as bad input"), haiku-2's finding 3 ("turns any bug into `:invalid`") and sonnet-1's finding 2 ("It hides real bugs ... as `{:error, :invalid}`") treat the rescue only as hiding bugs, so they do not count, as 2026-10-23 judged haiku-2. Haiku-1's magic 120 counts through finding 1's fix `update_change(:age, &min(&1, @max_age))`, which names the attribute. Sonnet-2's counts through finding 3's "with `@max_age` as a named attribute". Sonnet-1's `min(age, 120)` does not count. Haiku-2's `18` and `120` stay literals (lines 93, 95). Haiku-2's finding 13 names only the missing supervisor, and its fix does not build the email first, so the closure copy is unreported; the code's line 71 fixes it silently. Sonnet-1 finding 10 names the copy ("the closure copies the whole `user`"), and the code builds the email first, so it counts. Haiku-1 finding 8 ("nesting goes four levels deep") counts for the nesting. Haiku-2 names no nesting.

False positives: sonnet-1 finding 7 and sonnet-2 finding 9 put must-not-report line 27 `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]` under the `and`/`or`/`not` rule beside line 21. Neither changes a verdict, since both report line 21, and neither puts `and` or `not` on a nil-able option. Opus-1 (finding 11), haiku-1 (finding 9) and haiku-2 (finding 9) treat line 27 only as overlapping options, so this sweep has no line 27 false positive on Opus or Haiku, where every 2026-10-23 skill run had one. No run reports line 19, and every run keeps the line 11 why-comment (opus-1 line 98, haiku-1 line 93, haiku-2 line 91, sonnet-1 line 122, sonnet-2 line 105).

Rules outside the list, checked against their current text. The `->` rule: sonnet-2 lines 95-97 keep three one-line clauses where the first continues the computation and the others return finished errors, so it is listed under other_violations. The deciding sentence is "The body goes on the line after the `->` ... when the clauses do different kinds of work, one returning a finished value while another continues the computation, as in `value_end/3` below". Sonnet-1's `case Integer.parse` (lines 110-116) already puts each body on its own line. The `with` rule: opus-1 line 88, haiku-1 line 63 and haiku-2 line 64 are one-step `with`s whose body is a one-line `if` side effect and `{:ok, user}`, with no `else`. The new sentence "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through" allows them, so the kind of listing the 2026-10-23 sonnet-1 grade made does not apply. Both sonnets' `with`s have two or three steps. `do:`, captures and `fn` bodies: every `do:` body is one expression on the head's line, and every `fn` holds one call. Multi-line arguments: the sonnets build `attrs` under a name before the call. Module attributes hold literals. Sonnet-1 compiles with an unused-variable warning, listed under 'Before you finish'. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 call an unaliased `Mailer`, as the input does. No rule names that pattern, and neither review reports it, so it is not listed.

Format check: each review.md's elixir blocks were extracted to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-sweep-2026-10-31/code-review-skill/blocks/<run>-block<N>.ex. Elixir 1.20.3's `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0 on every importer block and every changeset sketch. The one exception is sonnet-1's block1, a schema sketch, which fails only because a bare file lacks Ecto's `locals_without_parens` for `field` and `schema`. With a .formatter.exs giving those (ectofmt/), it exits 0. A misformatted control (bad.ex) exits 1. So format_ok is true for all five.

No-options check: each importer was run against real Ecto 3.14.2 (Mix.install) by /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-suazi-Repos-idiomatic-elixir-skill/63fbd3f7-5995-424e-b268-7679cfbb08c1/scratchpad/grade-scratch-sweep-2026-10-31/code-review-skill/drive/run.exs, using common.exs (an `Accounts.Repo.insert/1` stub that applies the changeset action, plus `Mailer` and `Accounts.Mailer` stubs that message the driver) and a real `Accounts.TaskSupervisor`. `Accounts.User` is a schema with email, age, role (`Ecto.Enum`), nickname and name. For haiku-1 and haiku-2 it wraps the run's own `import_changeset/2`, and for sonnet-1 the run's own schema and `changeset/2`. For sonnet-2 it carries the `changeset/2` its line 3 assumes (cast of the four fields, `validate_number` at 18, `unique_constraint(:email)`); opus-1 builds its changeset in the importer. In all five, `import_user(%{"email" => "Ann@Example.com", "age" => "130", "role" => "admin"})` with no options returns `{:ok, user}` with age 120 and a lowercased email, and sends no mail. With `notify: true` it delivers exactly one email. An age of 17, an unknown role, a missing role and age "abc" each return `{:error, _}`. The only compiler warning in the runs' code is sonnet-1's unused `role` (its review.md line 94). The other warnings come from the grader's wrapper schemas. The stub Repo has no database, so `unique_constraint/3` was not exercised.

Compared with the 2026-10-23 skill grade, per_rule changes in seven of the 15 earlier rows. Haiku goes from clean to violated on the required-keys rule (haiku-2's `Map.get/2` on the struct), 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...' (haiku-2 misses the nesting), 'Return {:ok, value}...' (both haikus miss the line 8 raise) and 'Send processes only the data they need' (haiku-2 misses the copy). (both sonnets miss the magic 18, sonnet-1 also the 120), and from violated to clean on 'Send processes only the data they need'. Sonnet stays violated on the pipeline rule (sonnet-2 misses the line 12 pipe, as 2026-10-23's sonnet-1 did). Opus again breaks no graded rule and reports all 21 problems. The new 'Name a step...' rule is clean in every tier.
